evidence: Exactly two packages ('minbpe' and 'tests') with shallow directory depth (max 2), indicating a flat but modular structure
Clear separation of concerns: base tokenizer abstraction, basic tokenizer, regex tokenizer, and GPT-4 tokenizer in dedicated modules
Strong cohesion within modules (e.g., base.py contains Tokenizer base class and utility functions; gpt4.py contains tokenization logic extending RegexTokenizer)
Low fan-out (avg 2.0) suggests modules depend on few internal components and avoid tight cross-module coupling
No external service calls or HTTP clients detected; all logic is in-process
Tests reside in separate top-level module but import directly from the main package (no ports/adapters interfaces)
Inheritance hierarchy (BasicTokenizer → RegexTokenizer → GPT4Tokenizer) supports reuse within a single deployable unit
risks: GPT4Tokenizer has external dependency on tiktoken (runtime coupling could evolve toward microservices if external service abstraction grows)
Strong inheritance chain may hinder future testability or composition flexibility (e.g., if new tokenizer strategies emerge)
